newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit steady in thin trading ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit steady in thin trading ahead of weekend.

text.p: The ringgit was rangebound in late Asian trading on lack of interest ahead of the weekend, dealers said on Friday.
They said interest from buyers and sellers was well balanced, which restricted movement in dollar/ringgit for most of the day.
"Dollar/ringgit is in a consolidation phase after the strong movements recently," said a Malaysian bank dealer.
They said ringgit continued to be in demand from Kuala Lumpur corporate buyers and some overseas funds. This balanced selling pressure from other players in the market.
"Dollar/ringgit is supported because of cross-selling by U.S. funds against Sing dollar," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
A dealer with a U.S bank in Singapore said fear of Bank Negara's intervention above 2.51 and dollar sales by Malaysian corporates above 2.5080 was keeping dollar/ringgit subdued.
"The market is consolidating because there is interest from both sides," he added.
Dealers said the market was biding its time before attempting to test 2.5120, the level at which Bank Negara had intervened on Wednesday.
At 0930 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5036/46 a dollar.
